NH has also been a proud recipient of Frost & Sullivan India Healthcare Excellence Awards 2012 in the category Healthcare Service Provider Company of the Year and FICCI Health Care Excellence Award 2012 for Addressing Industry Issues. Job Purpose: ICU nurses are specialized, trained nurse professionals working with patients who have life-threatening situations that required an extended hospital stay in an intensive care or critical care unit of the hospital. The ICU nurse must be skilled to make complex assessments, give the patient intense therapy and provide intervention care. The nurse may also perform ongoing duties for a patient in ICU unit during his stay. Job Responsibilities: Patient Care Admission, discharge & transfer of patients. Individualized assessment is made by the ICU nurse to determine the immediate needs of the critical care patient. Ongoing assessment is then established to keep tabs on the patient's condition and make any changes in treatment based on hospital policy, procedure and protocol. Assessment helps the nurse and other hospital staff determines what plan of action to take in care of the patient. Assessment also allows the ICU nurse to educate the patient and her family on what to expect in the days, weeks and months following ICU treatment. Following doctor or head nurse instructions, the ICU nurse performs treatments and therapies for the patient. She gives the patient all necessary medication. If the patient lapses into cardiac arrest or another condition that requires resuscitation, the nurse follow hospital protocols and administers life-saving techniques. When a patient's condition changes rapidly, the nurse makes quick decisions to treat the patient effectively. As shift changes occur, it is the nurse's duty to inform the relief nurse of all patient care information. If the patient requires special procedures, the ICU nurse acts as an assistant to the doctor or head nurse. Documentation of assessments and drug therapy is recorded by the ICU nurse. She also makes documentation of physical therapy and other treatments given. The nurse must also keep all patient clinical records with doctor orders confidentially secure. The ICU nurse must be no discrimination and nonjudgmental when dealing with patients. In some cases, the ICU nurse is the team leader on the nursing staff and reports directly to the head or charg

title: Staff Nurse
description: Individualized assessment is made by the MICU/CCU/ITU nurse to determine the immediate needs of the critical care patient. Ongoing assessment is then established to keep tabs on the patient's condition and make any changes in treatment based on hospital policy, procedure and protocol. Assessment helps the nurse and other hospital staff determines what plan of action to take in care of the patient. Assessment also allows the CCU/MICU/ITU nurse to educate the patient and her family on what to expect in the days, weeks and months following CCU/MICU/ITU treatment. Following doctor or head nurse instructions, the CCU/MICU/ITU nurse performs treatments and therapies for the patient. She gives the patient all necessary medication. If the patient lapses into cardiac arrest or another condition that requires resuscitation, the nurse follow hospital protocols and administers life-saving techniques. When a patient's condition changes rapidly, the nurse makes quick decisions to treat the patient effectively. As shift changes occur, it is the nurse's duty to inform the relief nurse of all patient care information. If the patient requires special procedures, the CCU/MICU/ITU nurse acts as an assistant to the doctor or head nurse. Documentation of assessments and drug therapy is recorded by the CCU/MICU/ITU nurse. She also makes documentation of physical therapy and other treatments given. The nurse must also keep all patient clinical records with doctor orders confidentially secure. The CCU/MICU/ITU nurse must be no discriminative and nonjudgmental when dealing with patients. In some cases, the ICU nurse is the team leader on the nursing staff and reports directly to the head or charge nurse. In this position, she has the duty of directing and developing the skills and abilities of the staff under her. She is also responsible for giving the team assignments as directed by the head nurse. The nurse plays an active role in team conferences, participating in in-service trainings and initiating CPR and codes classes when needed.

She also makes documentation of physical therapy and other treatments given. The nurse must also keep all patient clinical records with doctor orders confidentially secure. description: Individualized assessment is made by the ICU nurse to determine the immediate needs of the critical care patient. Ongoing assessment is then established to keep tabs on the patient's condition and make any changes in treatment based on hospital policy, procedure and protocol. Assessment helps the nurse and other hospital staff determines what plan of action to take in care of the patient. Assessment also allows the ICU nurse to educate the patient and her family on what to expect in the days, weeks and months following ICU treatment. Following doctor or head nurse instructions, the ICU nurse performs treatments and therapies for the patient. She gives the patient all necessary medication. If the patient lapses into cardiac arrest or another condition that requires resuscitation, the nurse follow hospital protocols and administers life-saving techniques. When a patient's condition changes rapidly, the nurse makes quick decisions to treat the patient effectively. As shift changes occur, it is the nurse's duty to inform the relief nurse of all patient care information. If the patient requires special procedures, the ICU nurse acts as an assistant to the doctor or head nurse. Documentation of assessments and drug therapy is recorded by the ICU nurse. She also makes documentation of physical therapy and other treatments given. The nurse must also keep all patient clinical records with doctor orders confidentially secure. The ICU nurse must be no discriminative and nonjudgmental when dealing with patients. In some cases, the ICU nurse is the team leader on the nursing staff and reports directly to the head or charge nurse. In this position, she has the duty of directing and developing the skills and abilities of the staff under her. She is also responsible for giving the team assignments as directed by the head nurse. The nurse plays an active role in team conferences, participating in in-service trainings and initiating CPR and codes classes when needed.

title: Senior Registrar
description: Senior Registrar – Orthopaedic Surgery Position Details Job Title: Senior Registrar – Orthopaedic Surgery Department: Orthopaedics Reporting To: Consultant / Head of Department – Orthopaedics Location: Mazumdar Shaw Medical Centre Employment Type: Full-time Job Purpose To provide high-quality clinical care to patients with orthopaedic conditions, support consultants in the diagnosis and management of patients, participate in elective and emergency surgical services, and ensure safe, efficient and evidence-based delivery of orthopaedic care. Key Responsibilities 1. Clinical Responsibilities Assess and manage patients presenting with acute, chronic, traumatic and degenerative orthopaedic conditions. Conduct comprehensive history-taking and physical examinations. Formulate appropriate differential diagnoses and treatment plans under consultant supervision. Review investigations including X-rays, CT scans, MRI and laboratory reports. Participate in inpatient rounds, outpatient clinics and emergency services. Monitor postoperative patients and identify complications at an early stage. Provide appropriate preoperative and postoperative care. Manage orthopaedic emergencies including fractures, dislocations, acute limb injuries and other trauma-related conditions. Perform procedures within the scope of training and hospital privileges. 2. Surgical Responsibilities Assist consultants in elective and emergency orthopaedic procedures. Participate in fracture fixation, arthroplasty, arthroscopy, trauma surgery and other procedures appropriate to the department's scope of practice. Perform procedures independently only when appropriately credentialed and authorized. Ensure appropriate preoperative assessment, consent, investigations and surgical planning. Participate in postoperative monitoring and management. Maintain strict adherence to surgical safety protocols, including WHO Surgical Safety Checklist requirements.

Key Responsibilities Evaluate and manage preoperative and postoperative cardiac surgery patients. Assist in and progressively perform cardiothoracic surgical procedures under consultant supervision. Manage patients in the Cardiac ICU, wards, outpatient department (OPD), and emergency department. Participate in emergency surgeries and on-call duties. Perform procedures such as: Chest tube insertion and management Central venous catheter placement Arterial line insertion Temporary pacing wire management Wound care and postoperative management Interpret investigations including ECG, echocardiography reports, chest X-rays, CT scans, and relevant laboratory tests. Coordinate with anesthesiology, cardiology, perfusionists, intensivists, and nursing teams. Teach undergraduate and postgraduate students and participate in academic activities. Maintain accurate medical records and comply with hospital protocols. Participate in clinical audits, quality improvement initiatives, and research activities. Eligibility MBBS with MS/DNB in General Surgery or MCh/DNB/DrNB in Cardiothoracic & Vascular Surgery (depending on the institution's recruitment rules). Eligibility varies by hospital and whether the post is in a superspecialty department. Required Skills Knowledge of cardiothoracic surgical principles Critical care and ICU management Surgical assisting and procedural skills Emergency decision-making Teamwork and communication Basic research and teaching abilities

title: Senior Resident
description: Senior Resident – Adult Cardiology Department Cardiology Reports To Professor / Head of Department, Cardiology Job Summary The Senior Resident in Adult Cardiology is responsible for providing comprehensive inpatient and outpatient cardiac care under the supervision of consultant cardiologists. The role involves the evaluation, diagnosis, and management of adult patients with cardiovascular diseases, participation in emergency cardiac services, performance of diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, and active involvement in academic and research activities. Key Responsibilities Clinical Responsibilities Assess, diagnose, and manage patients with acute and chronic cardiovascular diseases. Provide care in outpatient clinics, inpatient wards, coronary care unit (CCU), and intensive care settings. Participate in emergency and on-call cardiac services, including the management of acute coronary syndromes, arrhythmias, heart failure, and cardiac emergencies. Perform detailed cardiovascular history taking, physical examination, and formulation of treatment plans. Interpret ECGs, echocardiograms, Holter monitoring, stress tests, and other non-invasive cardiac investigations. Assist in and perform cardiac procedures as per institutional protocols and competency, including temporary pacemaker insertion, pericardiocentesis, central venous access, and other bedside procedures. Assist in cardiac catheterization, coronary angiography, angioplasty, device implantation, and electrophysiology procedures as required. Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation. Academic Responsibilities Participate in departmental academic activities, including seminars, journal clubs, case presentations, and clinical discussions. Teach and supervise junior residents, interns, and medical students. Participate in continuing medical education (CME) programs and departmental training initiatives.

title: Senior Registrar
description: Job Description: Senior Resident – Vascular & Endovascular Surgery Position Senior Resident – Department of Vascular & Endovascular Surgery Department Vascular & Endovascular Surgery Reporting To Head of Department (HOD) Consultant Vascular & Endovascular Surgeons Job Summary The Senior Resident in Vascular & Endovascular Surgery is responsible for providing comprehensive inpatient, outpatient, emergency, operative, and perioperative care for patients with vascular diseases. The role includes assisting and independently performing procedures according to competency level, participating in emergency services, academic activities, research, and teaching undergraduate and postgraduate trainees. Responsibilities typically include managing arterial, venous, and lymphatic disorders using both open surgical and endovascular techniques under consultant supervision. Key Responsibilities Clinical Responsibilities Evaluate and manage patients in OPD, IPD, ICU, and Emergency. Perform detailed history taking, clinical examination, diagnosis, and treatment planning. Manage vascular emergencies including: Acute limb ischemia Aortic emergencies Vascular trauma Dialysis access complications Deep vein thrombosis Conduct preoperative and postoperative patient care. Participate in daily ward rounds with consultants. Maintain accurate clinical documentation and electronic medical records. Operative Responsibilities Assist and progressively perform procedures under supervision including: Peripheral arterial bypass surgery Carotid endarterectomy AV fistula creation and revision Varicose vein surgery Lower limb amputations Vascular access procedures Diagnostic angiography Peripheral angioplasty Stenting procedures Thrombectomy and thrombolysis Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR/TEVAR) assistance Hybrid vascular procedures according to competency. Endovascular Responsibilities Assist in catheter-based vascular interventions. Interpret CT angiography, MR angiography, Doppler ultrasound, and conventional angiography. Participate in pre-procedure planning. Learn radiation safety and contrast management. Assist in device selection and deployment during interventions. Academic Responsibilities Present seminars, journal clubs, and case discussions. Participate in mortality and morbidity meetings. Attend departmental academic sessions. Teach MBBS students, junior residents, and nursing staff. Participate in CME programs and conferences. Senior residents often take leadership roles in organising conferences and case discussions
